scores.reason: Verified at head: `export function usePermissions(projectId, permissions)` is a generic name where B.8 asks for `use<Feature>Permissions(projectId)` (useKeyManagerPermissions); SecretModals.tsx/ContainerModals.tsx/OrderModals.tsx bundle several modals while B.12 wants `<Verb><Resource>Modal.tsx`; `utils.ts`/`constants.ts` are generic. Naming rule violation with no user-facing effect, so Low.
Same problem as C16 (hook named usePermissions); C16 covers it and more.

B.13 and Quick Reject name import order: SecretsList.tsx puts `@/client/trpcClient` after the Juno import block (tRPC must come before Juno), and uses `../../-components/usePermissions` although B.13 says all imports must use `@/` aliases with no `../../` traversal. Verified; no runtime effect.

Strings such as `Create Secret`, `Sort by`, `Search by name...` and the column arrays are plain English in packages/aurora, but the review standards (B.14, What NOT to Review) say hardcoded strings there are lint-enforced and not a finding; that scope wins.

Issue #1133 spec lists Orders columns Name / ID, Type, Status; head has `ORDERS_COLUMNS = ["ID", "Status", "Type", ""]` and the row renders no order name/reference. Secrets and Containers match the spec (column order aside, deliberate). A criterion partly delivered, so Low.

B.6 says to distinguish empty reasons (no data suggests creating, no filter results suggests clearing filters). SecretListContainer has one empty state, `No Secrets Found` / `Create one to get started.`, and SecretsList passes it no search value, so a search with no hits gets the create hint. Wording only, so Low.

Verified: `<Status status="error" title={error?.message ?? t`Failed to Load Secrets`} />` with no body or retry, same in DetailsViews. B.6 asks for a course of action only 'where feasible' and the message does give some explanation, so this is a nitpick, not a clear Reject.
